correctness.rationale: The proof diagonalizes TT†, a strictly positive Jacobi Toeplitz matrix, with normalized discrete sine eigenvectors and strictly distinct positive eigenvalues. Its ± singular-vector pairs contribute 2(g−1) nodes from the divisibility equivalence (M+1)|rk for every lossy index, and the unique A-only zero mode contributes one. For any G eigenvector, Re eigenvalue is exactly minus half its rate-weighted lossy-site weight, so undamped modes are precisely the clean nodes; their reducing subspace and finite-dimensional spectral complement prove genuine convergence of the survival norm. Summing paired projections gives 2/(M+1) times the sine-square sum, which is zero or g/(M+1) via roots of unity. All rates/hoppings strictly positive and S nonempty; edge M=1 and g=1 are consistent. Reproduction: python artifacts/verify.py reports VERIFY_OK for 2343 finite spectral cases and selected long-time exponentials. Numerical evidence is corroborative, not the all-size proof.

value.rationale: Boundary-state preparation is a motivated open-quantum-system problem. Loss at arbitrary B positions may preserve many additional nonzero-frequency dark modes rather than only the topological zero mode; the gcd provides a complete placement design criterion g=1 for a unique energy-dark mode. The exact long-time probability for a local B-site input is a nontrivial, rate- and hopping-independent two-level residue law, with natural relevance to designing or diagnosing sparse dissipative traps. This is an all-size sharp classification of a physically standard chain, not an arbitrary unmotivated finite-table recomputation. No claim about interacting many-body steady states or quantitative hardware lifetime is made.
